business.summary: Green Basket Market is a single grocery shop in Dublin moving into neighbourhood delivery (a second shop may follow later). Customers order from about 1,500 products through a phone app, choosing a two-hour delivery slot and paying by card; shop staff pack orders from a shared tablet website at the packing bench, weighing loose items and applying the customer's substitution choice; a shop manager controls prices, offers and stock; two part-time drivers use an app to see their route and confirm delivery with a photo. Orders move through clear stages from placed to delivered, with rules for cancellation, refunds, delivery fees, a fixed delivery area and VAT-inclusive pricing.

actors.name: Customer
actors.does: Browses about 1,500 products by aisle, builds a basket, picks a two-hour delivery slot, pays by card, tracks the order, and can repeat a previous order with one tap.

actors.name: Shop staff
actors.does: Uses a tablet website at the packing bench to see new orders in pick order, tick off items, weigh loose products, apply the customer's advance substitution choice, and mark the order ready.

actors.name: Shop manager
actors.does: Sets prices, offers and stock, and switches products off when they run out.

actors.name: Driver
actors.does: Sees their delivery route on an app, opens each address in a maps application, and marks an order delivered with a photo of where the bags were left; calls the customer if they are not at home.

actors.name: Accountant
actors.does: Receives the daily sales sheet by e-mail and will provide the VAT rules per product category.

rules: Delivery slots are two-hour windows between 8:00 and 20:00; same-day delivery is available if ordered before 15:00.
Products sold by weight (e.g. fruit, deli) are packed between 960 g and 1.1 kg for a 1 kg order; the card is charged the real weighed amount but never more than 10% above the price the customer saw.
A customer can cancel an order until packing starts.
If the shop cannot deliver an order, the customer gets a full refund.
Delivery fee is 3.50 EUR, free for baskets above 60 EUR.
Delivery is only available to about 12 listed postcodes; nothing outside that area.
Card is authorised at checkout and charged when the order is packed.
Prices include VAT; some food is zero-rated and some is 13.5%, with exact rules per product category to be given by the accountant.
A daily sales sheet is e-mailed to the owner and the accountant.
Customers log in with a text-message code (OTP).
A push notification is sent when the order is packed and when the driver is on the way.
An e-mail receipt is sent to the customer.
If the customer is not at home, the driver calls them.
No live map tracking of the driver is needed in the first version.
Each customer chooses in advance, per product, 'replace with similar' or 'do not replace' for substitutions.
The packing bench tool must be a website, not an installable app, because tablets are shared.
jobs: Daily sales sheet e-mailed to the owner and the accountant.
existing: A product list in a spreadsheet with barcodes and photos, kept in a shared folder.
No website yet for the shop.

modules.name: Green Basket Market API
modules.why: Stores products, orders, slots, stock, payments and drives notifications and the daily sales job.

modules.name: Customer App
modules.why: Lets customers browse products, build a basket, choose a delivery slot, pay by card, track orders and repeat past orders.

modules.name: Driver App
modules.why: Shows each driver their route, opens addresses in a maps application, and lets them mark delivery with a photo.

modules.name: Shop Manager Panel
modules.why: Lets the manager set prices, offers and stock, and switch products off.

sdks.title: SMS login codes
sdks.why: Customers log in using a text-message code.

sdks.title: Push and e-mail notifications
sdks.why: Push when the order is packed and when the driver is on the way; e-mail receipts; and the daily sales sheet e-mail.

sdks.title: Card payments
sdks.why: Authorises at checkout, charges on packing, and refunds when delivery is not possible.

open_questions.question: Should customers be charged extra when a substitution item costs more than the original product?
open_questions.why: The document explicitly says this is undecided and it affects pricing and payment rules.
open_questions.proposed_default: Do not charge extra for substitutions; the shop absorbs the cost difference.

open_questions.question: If alcohol is sold, how should age verification be handled (ID check at the door, proof-of-age process, etc.)?
open_questions.why: The document says this is undecided and it affects what the driver app and order flow need to support.
open_questions.proposed_default: No alcohol sold until an ID-check process is defined; driver checks ID manually at the door once added.

open_questions.question: Should the system include a loyalty points programme?
open_questions.why: The document says this is undecided and it would affect the customer app and data model.
open_questions.proposed_default: No loyalty programme in the first version.

open_questions.question: What are the exact VAT rules (zero-rated vs 13.5%, or other rates) per product category?
open_questions.why: The document says the accountant will supply these later, but they are needed for pricing and the daily sales sheet.
open_questions.proposed_default: Each product gets a VAT category field, to be filled in by the accountant before launch.

open_questions.question: Which SMS provider should send the login codes?
open_questions.why: The document asks for text-message login codes but names no provider.

open_questions.question: Which push notification and e-mail providers should be used?
open_questions.why: The document asks for push notifications and e-mail receipts/reports but names no providers.
open_questions.proposed_default: fcm for push notifications, sendgrid for e-mail.

open_questions.question: Which card payment gateway should process payments?
open_questions.why: The document requires card payments, authorisation at checkout and refunds, but names no payment gateway.

open_questions.question: Which storage provider should host the driver's delivery photos?
open_questions.why: The document requires a delivery photo to be stored but names no storage provider.

open_questions.question: Should Polish be supported from the first version, or added later as the document suggests ('maybe Polish later')?
open_questions.why: The intent is uncertain and affects scope and timeline for the customer app.
open_questions.proposed_default: English only for v1; add Polish in a later release.

open_questions.question: Should the system be designed to support multiple shop locations from the start, since a second shop is mentioned as a future possibility?
open_questions.why: A second shop is mentioned as a future plan, which could affect how products, stock and orders are modelled.
open_questions.proposed_default: Design for a single shop in v1; add multi-location support later if needed.

open_questions.question: Which hosting provider, database and cache should be used for the server, admin panel and staff website?
open_questions.why: The document does not mention any hosting, database or cache technology.
open_questions.proposed_default: docker-server host with a postgres database and a redis cache for the server; simple web hosting for the admin panel and staff website.
